Empire, on her downward trip from Albany, met

There being dense fog at the time, the pilot mis-
calculated his course, and ran her at least twenty
feet through the wharf at the foot of Nineteenth
street, smashing her stem and injuring her bottom
little. As she was going at considerable speed,
the conclusion was very violent, and great confu
sion prevailed on board for some minutes amongst
the passengers, who were taken on board the
Knckerbocker, which came alongside shortly after
wards, and conveyed them in safety to the city
The Empire has been taken of, and has gone
round to be repaired IN the East River.

FRoLIc WITH SHARK T'hurlO,o HteG in
one Of his late letters from Santa Cruz, gives
the subjoined account of rencontre with that
dangerous isii-the powerful shark:


Tho uarauding dreaded Shark, always rife
in tropical climates, is so common here as to
deprive US of the luxury of open sea bathing.
The negro conc divers disregard these mon
sters; and some of the planters battle after send
ing negro further out into the sea as senti-
mel.


We had a rare frolic with shark few days
since. Spanish schooner came in here with
ca tie. The cattle had been several days upon
short allowance of water, and in swimming
them ashore III their weakened condition, two
of them died. One of the carcasses was taken
by the negroes and anchored half mile from
the shore, TO bait sharks with. The rascals
soon made their appearance. The harpoon
was sent with sure aim at a huge fellow, who
darted off with such force as to break the line.
But three of the school soon returned, one of
which was struck with better fortune. This
one, after powerful but unavaing struggles to
escape, rose to the surface Of the water, and
then the negroes got Ground hitch" upon his
tail, when they pulled for the shore. The word
was passed through the streets that a shark
was coming in This drew large concourse
of white, 0ringed, speckled, and gray" spirits
10 the beach.


When the boat approached the shore, 4 nc
gro landed with the line to which the shark
was fast and which was seized by men, women
and boys, who with infinite glee, drew the COM
mon enemy, struggling and floundering, with
blood streaming from his side and nostrils, high
and dry upon land. This shark was eight feet
long, and though the harpoon had gone deep
into his vitals, he displayed an activity and
strength which admonished us to keep at a re-
spectful distance. Its skin is smooth and sleek
like that Of seal, or porpoise, and but for its
enormous mouth, you would suppose it quite
as harmless. After forcing its mouth open
with handspike, and thrusting large stene
into his NAV, it was cut open for its liver,
which yielded seven gallons of lamp oil. But
the shark had within him the evidence Of hav-
ing feasted beautifully upon unroasted beef be.
fore the harpoon did its Office Not less than
thirty pounds of raw beef dropt from under his
gasket Among other delicate bits was a sur
lon weighing twelve or fifteen pounds, with
two entire and still unbroken ribs. During
this process the shark foundered with prodi-
gious strength, and even after its vtals were
all out, the body retained spasmodc action
and finally, when the negroes rolled the trunk
back into the sea its native element seemed tc
impart sort of life, for the contortions contin
ued until il sunk out of sight.

A GERMAN NEUTRALITY-SUSPICIOUS. June


20. During the last ten years there has not


been any capital execution in our city. The
day before yesterday the scatiold was erected
for the decapitation of young woman named


Margaret Rudhardt, who was sentenced to
death for poisoning her husband with arsenic


This act Of supreme justice was marked by
strange incident:-The execution here takes
place with u sword. The cuprit is placed on
his knees, with white handkerchief over his
eyes; one of the eXecutoner's assistants then
lies down before the culprt, seizes him with
his two hands by the thighs, and keeps him inn
novably fixed to the ground, whilst another
holds him by the hair, and draws his head back,
so that the muscles of the neck be extended


when the executioner, with his sword, which
he grasps with both hands, cuts off the head


At the moment when the latter was about to


niiict the fatal blow on Margaret Rudhardt, a
man rushed through the compact crowd that
surrounded the scat1old, crying out in u stento-
Tian voice, "Stop. stop!" and waving at the
same time over his head white handkerchief


The cxecutioner instnctively dropped his ARM


his aids looscned the victim, removed the band
age from her eyes, and Margaret Rudhardt,
who during those awful preparations had ex-
hibted good deal of calmness, rose smiling


for the unhappy woman as we'll as the execu-
toner and everybody ,-including the recorder
of the Royal Court of Stuttgart, who was on
the platform drawing up the minutes of the exc
cution, -belleved that she had been pardoned
This, however, was not the case. The author
iof the incident was arrested, and it was soon
discovered that he had been an ole servant of
Margaret Rudhardt's father, who imagined
that, by interrupting the execution, it would


be retarded, and that the daughter of his lor-
inner master would then have a chance of OBJ
flaming her pardon. After an interval of half
an hour, which was painful respite for Mar
garet Rudhardt, she was again obliged to kneel,
and Justice had its course. The crowd, al
though much moved by the spectacle, observ-
| ed the greatest order, and shortly afterwards
silently dispersed.-[ Paris paper.
